title: Balanced Order Expressions

statement.md: Pricing formulas use three bracket kinds: `()`, `[]` and `{}`. For each expression decide whether the brackets are balanced: every opening bracket is closed by the same kind in the correct order. All other characters are ignored.

If the expression is balanced print `OK`. Otherwise print `ERR i` where $i$ is the **1-based position of the first character that proves it is wrong**: a closing bracket with no matching opener on top of the stack, or a closing bracket of the wrong kind. If the scan ends with unclosed openers, print `ERR i` where $i$ is the position of the **earliest unclosed** opening bracket.

inputFormat: First line: $q$. Then $q$ lines, each one expression (it may be empty, and may contain spaces).
constraints: Total length of all expressions at most $10^6$
hints: Push the position of each opener. On a closer, check the top of the stack.
At the end, the earliest unclosed opener is the bottom of the stack.

editorial.md: One stack scan, $O(n)$. A closer fails if the stack is empty or the top has a different kind. If the scan finishes with a non-empty stack, the earliest unclosed opener is the first element pushed that is still there, which is the bottom of the stack.
